 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AC-7611, alleging that on 13.03.2023 at 9.40 a.m., when riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-EN-8377 on Hosur road NH-44 (service road), in front of South End Hotel, within the limits of Hebbagodi police station, driver of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51- AC-7611 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to Motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Narayana Health City hospital, Bengaluru and Medicare Hospital,
V.V.Puram, Bengaluru.
3.
As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged about 45 years, used to earn Rs.98,000/- p.m. by working as Junior Training Officer in ITI College, Hosur road, Bengaluru.
4. Regarding the accident, Hebbagodi police registered crime No.124/2023.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 owner of the Canter Lorry appeared through his Advocate, however, neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. In response to the notice, respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through his advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 15.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 13.03.2023 at about 09.40 a.m., on Bengaluru - Hosur NH-44 (service road) in front of South End Hotel, in view of the negligent use of the Truck bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AC-7611 accident taken place resulting in the Vinod K N vs Jyothi Concrete Blocks on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164080909/
2 injuries to the petitioner?
2.

8. On 22.01.2025, 05.03.2025, 05.04.2025 petitioner deposed as P.W.1 and produced 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13.
9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative.
Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.1,01,087/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- In the evidence petitioner stated that on on 13.03.2023 at 9.40 a.m., when riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-EN-8377 on the service road of Hosur road NH-44, in front of South End Hotel, within the limits of Hebbagodi police station, driver of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AC-7611 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to Motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
12. In the written statement respondent No.2- Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

13. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated that when he was riding Motorcycle from Dairy circle towards Bommasandra, accident taken place and place of accident is a two way traffic area without divider.
Petitioner stated that during accident, no vehicles are running in front of his two wheeler and a Lorry which came from the opposite direction caused accident.
P.W.1 submitted ignorance to the question whether in the place of accident, 2 four wheelers can pass simultaneously.
P.W.1 admitted that head on collision taken place between his two wheeler bike and Lorry.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.124/2023 registered by Hebbagodi police against driver of Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AC-7611 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC, on the basis of complaint presented by Rahul, S/o.Balaraj R., pillion rider of the Motorcycle.

Ex.P.2 is the copy of Charge Sheet filed by Hebbagodi police in Cr.No.124/2023 against Ramesha Hanumappa Pujari, S/o.Hanumappa, driver of Canter Lorry Vinod K N vs Jyothi Concrete Blocks on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164080909/
3 bearing No.KA-51- AC-7611 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Motor vehicles Accident Report.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of Wound Certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as alleged history of RTA (2 wheeler Vs. Lorry), patient was the rider of the 2 wheeler, near Bommasandra at 9.40 a.m. on 13.03.2023.
15. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

16. Hence, I have concluded that on 13.03.2023 at 9.40 a.m., when petitioner was riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-EN-8377 on service road of Hosur road, NH-44, in front of South End Hotel,
within the limits of Hebbagodi police station, Ramesha Hanumappa Pujari negligently drove the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AC-7611, dashed the same to Motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner. Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered grievous injuries, took treatment at Narayana Health City hospital, Bengaluru and Medicare Hospital,
V.V.Puram, Bengaluru as an inpatient, underwent surgery by spending Rs.6,50,000/- for treatment.

Petitioner stated that, due to the injuries suffered in the accident, as per the advice of the doctor,
unable to attend duties for a period of two months.
18.
In the petition petitioner has stated that as on the date of accident, he used to earn Rs.98,000/-p.m. by working as Junior Training Officer in ITI College, Hosur road, Bengaluru.
19. In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

20. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.6,50,000/-
for treatment and non production of documents regarding spending of Rs.10,000/- towards repair of Motorcycle and loss of income (leave) for a period of two months.

21. Wound certificate, Discharge Summary, shows that in the accident petitioner suffered facial soft tissue injury, laceration over left eyebrow, forehead, took treatment at Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center.
Medical bills shows that petitioner spent approximately Rs.26,087 for treatment.
In the copy of the Aadhar Card, Driving Licence and PAN card, marked at Exs.P.10, P.11 and P.13, date of birth of petitioner is noted as 30.07.1978.

In this case petitioner has not produced documents regarding occupation, quantum of income, loss of leave etc.
22.

In this case respondents have not produced any type evidence to disbelieve the evidence of petitioner regarding nature and consequence of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken for those injuries.

23. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documentary evidence regarding occupation and income Vinod K N vs Jyothi Concrete Blocks on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164080909/

sentences.text:
of the petitioner, I award compensation under the following heads:
Sl
. No .
Heads of Compensation Amount (Rs.)
1) Pain and agony 40,000.00 2) Treatment charges 26,087.00 3) Conveyance, nourishment and 5,000.00 attendant charges 4) Loss of amenities and future 30,000.00 unhappiness:

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,01,087/-
with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
25. In the written statement, respondent No.2- Insurance Company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AC- 7611 as on the date of accident.
In the file, there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 owner of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA- 51-AC-7611 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51- AC-7611 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,01,087/- (Rupees One lakh one thousand eighty seven only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Canter Lorry bearing No.KA-51-AC-7611 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
